title: review: H7 fix round 2: test_flaky_rerun_then_escalate asserts the old pytest command while the rerun now uses the worktree's runner; align the assertion with the new command shape (test id present, timeout set) without weakening it (gate_red on T-0412)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain b9c2972, fb696ce and 4a605cc (T-0364, T-0412) in git log; never drop or amend them.
Gate red on T-0412 (daemon run): tests/test_daemon.py::Daemon::test_flaky_rerun_then_escalate fails with AssertionError: Lists differ: ['/Users/.../wt/T-0412/.venv/bin/python', ..., 'tests/test_x.py::test_x'] != ['pytest', '-q', 'tests/test_x.py::test_x']. Cause: 4a605cc made the flaky rerun use the worktree's own runner (per the T-0412 spec) but left the fb696ce assertion expecting the bare pytest command.
Fix: update the assertion in test_flaky_rerun_then_escalate to the new contract without weakening it: the rerun command runs only the failing ids (each id present exactly once in the argv, no full-suite discovery), is executed with cwd = the worktree, and carries a timeout equal to [daemon].flaky_rerun_timeout_s; keep the rest of the test (one rerun, kind flaky, both runs in resume_hint, escalation) unchanged. Confirm test_flaky_rerun_has_timeout_and_timeout_is_not_flaky still passes. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0 (whole suite), then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows 4a605cc, fb696ce and b9c2972 below your commit
tests/test_daemon.py::test_flaky_rerun_then_escalate passes and asserts the failing ids, the worktree cwd and the timeout of the rerun command
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: failure_kind() gates the flaky rerun with `len(runs) < min(1, rerun_max)`. min(1, rerun_max) is 1 for every rerun_max >= 1, so raising [daemon].flaky_rerun_max above 1 in pool.toml has no effect — the daemon still ever attempts exactly one rerun. Only rerun_max=0 (disable) actually changes behavior. This silently breaks the documented config knob; no test exercises rerun_max > 1. Should be `len(runs) < rerun_max`.
